learning_outcomes.text: Students should be able to understand, describe, and analyze fundamental phenomena of human movement.
Key aspects include the biomechanics of the musculoskeletal system and biomechanical principles.
Students can apply biomechanical methods for movement measurements and assess physical loads.
They can understand and optimally design human-machine or prosthesis interactions, as well as human-(sport)-equipment interactions.

syllabus_topics: Ergonomie beim Fahrradfahren, in Kraftfahrzeugen, im Büro und im Alltag
Gehen, Lauf, Sprinten ohne und mit Prothesen
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a graded oral or written examination, contributing 100% to the module grade.
